name: Howard Lutnick
role: U.S. Secretary of Commerce (since February 2025); former chairman and CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald
summary: Lutnick, a Wall Street executive, is a Trump ally who describes himself as fiscally conservative and socially liberal. His stated positions centre on tariffs and reshoring, a balanced budget, deregulation and energy production, and a more selective immigration system. As Commerce Secretary he has also pursued government equity in companies and negotiated investment-for-tariff-relief deals.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Mixed: said 'a lesser regulatory environment will unleash America' and wants permitting and mining rules cut, but also used tariff threats to force pharma 'most favored nation' pricing and urged audited, fully backed stablecoins and AI standards.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Said the aim is 'to stop letting people into the country without a clear benefit', criticised the green-card lottery as bringing in the 'bottom quartile', and replaced it in his pitch with the $1 million/$5 million Gold Card; supports H-1B only for high earners.

free-trade.rationale: Said 'there ain't no such thing' as free trade, blamed NAFTA for gutting Michigan and Ohio auto workers, called the post-war low-tariff era a mistake that should have ended decades ago, and described the US trade deficit as a ripoff.

nation-first.rationale: Defined America First as 'American citizens employed first' and said 'we care about America first, we care about American workers first... then we worry about Canada'.

open-borders.rationale: Said open immigration worked when America 'gave people nothing', but that with welfare, food stamps and housing 'you have to close the borders'; wants entry based on benefit to the country.

limit-growth.rationale: Goals are faster growth: predicted 4-6% GDP growth and 'an economy that is explosive', and wants regulation on mining and energy cut; he never proposed limiting growth for the environment.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Said of the Japan investment fund: 'Nuclear, we want to build a hundred billion dollars of nuclear plants. They will pay for it.'

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Argued that tariffs create 'reciprocity, fairness and respect' and that 'a thoughtful tariff policy that drives domestic manufacturing' is fundamental to American workers (hearing); as Secretary he ran the steel, aluminum, auto, pharmaceutical and semiconductor tariffs to bring production home and said 'if we blink, they will sell below cost in America and drive our domestic companies out of business'.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Personally negotiated Japan's $550 billion vehicle that finances 'any project we want to build in America' (nuclear plants as the example), tied tariff relief to pharma reshoring, named five strategic industries (steel/aluminum/copper, autos, chips, pharma, lumber) and pursued an equity stake in Intel for CHIPS money.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Called himself 'outcome driven' ('the outcomes are what matter') and described reading contracts rather than assuming 'a Republican will just rip that stuff up'; his own statement of method, not a general claim about policy ideology.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said the Panama Canal 'needs to come back under our oversight' (he researched it for Trump) and that Greenland 'is going to join America if the people in Greenland want to vote'; the Greenland case is framed as consent, so the answer is low.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Repeatedly framed a $2 trillion annual deficit as the problem and a balanced budget as the goal ('interest rates are going to come smashing down'); called the 2021 American Rescue Plan's $2 trillion 'unnecessary' and the source of inflation.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Said that with a welfare state 'you have to close the borders because... they need to give it to each other' and that people shouldn't be let in to 'leech off of us' on welfare, food stamps and housing; stated as history and policy rationale rather than a specific eligibility rule.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Said 'we need to drill and we need to drive down energy cost', 'we need fossil fuels for the next 30 and 40 years', and listed 'drill baby drill' as part of the plan; criticised Biden for closing oil wells and acreage.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Said 'I need a new Fed chair who cuts rates' and wants lower rates to reach 6% growth, which runs against insulating the Fed from the executive; he also says inflation comes only from printing money, a price-stability argument, so the evidence is mixed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Said he is a patent holder, wants to 'enhance their ability to get patents to protect them', to cut the patent backlog and to stop Chinese abuse of the patent and trademark systems; 'if you do not respect our companies' IP... you should not expect the same treatment here'.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Argued that US-backed stablecoin issuers 'must onboard US law enforcement' and give government AI tools access so illicit flows can be traced, noting an electronic dollar is 'much easier to catch'; addressed to stablecoins, not all payments.

notes: Employer positions (the Trump administration's) are counted only where he stated or personally drove them. Many topics (healthcare, social issues, civil liberties, foreign policy outside trade) have no recorded position by him and are null. Epstein and Tether/Cantor ties, the Social Security 'fraudster' remark and his vaccine remarks are controversies but match no statement here. The Gold Card and income-tax waiver ideas were not scored against tax statements.
